sources.bibliography: Hansen, P. R., Lunde, A., and Nason, J. M. (2011). The Model Confidence Set. Econometrica 79(2), 453–497.
sources.inspected_scope: Selected full-text passages: pp458–460 definitions and Theorem1; pp462–463 MCS p-values and mixing assumptions; pp464–465 local test discussion; p476 parameter uncertainty.
sources.supports: Coverage of all best models conditional on assumptions; exclusion p-values are membership thresholds, not a candidate-specific pair equality test.
sources.does_not_establish: Coverage of the supplied nested seed/time RMSE extension, finite R12 validity, or singleton power. The singleton candidate argument in README is an explicitly marked deduction.

sources.bibliography: Owen, A. B., and Eckles, D. (2012). Bootstrapping data arrays of arbitrary order. Annals of Applied Statistics 6(3), 895–927.
sources.inspected_scope: Electronic reprint: abstract and introduction; selected variance passages, and discussion p22 of PDF (printed electronic p22), including smooth functions of means. Reprint expressly differs in pagination from journal.
sources.supports: Product reweighting for crossed random effects and careful variance approximation; smooth transformations need a Taylor argument.
sources.does_not_establish: Validity for serially dependent temporal columns, nested mean-of-roots, arbitrary degeneracy or small seed count.

sources.bibliography: Menzel, K. (2021). Bootstrap With Cluster-Dependence in Two or More Dimensions. Econometrica 89(5), 2143–2188.
sources.inspected_scope: Abstract, introduction pp2143–2145, especially footnote1 p2143 and differentiable-function discussion p2145.
sources.supports: Multiway cluster inference may be non-Gaussian; sampling dimensions are independent. Weak serial dependence across time is explicitly outside this paper's treatment.
sources.does_not_establish: A theorem for the current dependent-calendar estimator. Its nonuniformity result should not be misquoted as impossibility of every restricted regular model.

sources.bibliography: Giacomini, R., and White, H. (2006). Tests of Conditional Predictive Ability. Econometrica 74(6), 1545–1578.
sources.inspected_scope: Published 2006 paper: pp1546–1550 distinction of conditional/unconditional targets and estimation design; Theorem1 pp1553–1554; §3.4 p1557 unconditional form and HAC growth.
sources.supports: Conditional null is stronger than equality on average; constant-information special case coincides with DM. Bounded rolling estimation windows or a fixed-estimation scheme have explicit roles.
sources.does_not_establish: A distinct third primary test merely by adding an instrument, nor random-training-seed nonlinear-risk validity. A separate eScholarship result was an April2003 working-paper version and was not silently substituted for 2006.

sources.bibliography: Clark, T. E., and West, K. D. (2007). Approximately normal tests for equal predictive accuracy in nested models. Journal of Econometrics 138(1), 291–311.
sources.supports: Actual nesting and adjustment of mean squared prediction errors for estimation noise are the stated setting.
sources.does_not_establish: Admissibility for arbitrary neural-architecture comparisons or mean individual RMSE. No full theorem review claimed.

sources.bibliography: Diebold, F. X., and Mariano, R. S. (1995). Comparing Predictive Accuracy. Journal of Business and Economic Statistics 13(3), 253–263.
sources.inspected_scope: Bibliographic front matter and indexed abstract; body PDF is an image scan without usable text extraction in web tool.
sources.supports: Original identity of the method only. The explicit mean-loss/HAC formula is cross-checked in primary GW2006 §3.4, not attributed to an unread DM theorem.

sources.bibliography: Harvey, D., Leybourne, S., and Newbold, P. (1997). Testing the equality of prediction mean squared errors. International Journal of Forecasting 13(2), 281–291.
sources.inspected_scope: Publisher metadata/abstract search result only; full paper inaccessible through attempted sources.
sources.supports: Bibliographic identification and MSPE focus only.
sources.does_not_establish: No claim of having inspected the small-sample derivation, its validity for t(R−1), or mixed seed/time degrees of freedom.

sources.bibliography: Politis, D. N., and Romano, J. P. (1994). The Stationary Bootstrap. Journal of the American Statistical Association 89(428), 1303–1313.
sources.inspected_scope: Publisher metadata and indexed primary-paper passages; PDF scan has no usable body text in web extraction.
sources.supports: Source of stationary temporal resampling; generic parameter extensions require conditions.
sources.does_not_establish: No inspected theorem for independently sampled training seeds crossed with a serial calendar; no exact finite-sample guarantee claimed.

sources.bibliography: Friedman, M. (1937). The Use of Ranks to Avoid the Assumption of Normality Implicit in the Analysis of Variance. Journal of the American Statistical Association 32(200), 675–701.
sources.inspected_scope: Original scan bibliographic page; no usable body text extraction.
sources.supports: Identity as rank-based original method only.
sources.does_not_establish: No claim of an inspected theorem supporting use on correlated daily origins or primary mean-RMSE equality. Rank/mean mismatch in README is an elementary logical argument.
